speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am aware that a great deal has already been said in this Chamber about gender inequality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: But, Mr Speaker, despite all of these words, there is still more that needs to be said and there is still more that needs to be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore, like every other country, remains deeply divided by gender, with gender having a visible and invisible impact on how every one of us live our life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Gender has an influence on the careers we choose, how much we get paid, our role in personal and professional relationships; our role as parents and caregivers; our ability to participate in decisions that affect our lives; our status in society; our safety at home and on the streets; our health; our finances; and our housing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are biologically different, and we are also different because of how we are raised and the roles, expectations and assumptions that society, culture and religion ascribe to gender.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, Mr Speaker, many of these differences are positive and need to be celebrated and reinforced.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I do not want to live in a world where men and women are identical to each other, as that would be dull, unproductive and inconsistent with many deeply held social, cultural and religious beliefs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Gender equality does not mean that men and women are the same.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: What it does mean is that a person's rights and opportunities do not depend on being male or female, but on their individual preferences, character and skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, as the Vice President of Singapore Muslim Women's Association (PPIS), an organisation that was formed in 1952, I have seen first-hand the transformative power of our efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, importantly, both men and women have a role to play in addressing gender inequality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Women cannot solve gender inequality without men and men cannot solve gender inequality without women.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This year, the International Women's Day campaign theme was "Inspire Inclusion".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While I agree with the campaign "that we need to understand and value women's inclusion", I do not believe that we can inspire or achieve inclusion, for women, if we do not include men in the conversation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to talk with men and boys, about gender and gender inequality, and have them as equal contributors as we build a culture of gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: If men are part of the problem – and sometimes they are – it makes sense to have them as part of the solution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This means that we are designing solutions with incomplete data.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It can also lead to men criticising or undermining gender equality and to men being excluded, abandoned or left behind in the debate about gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This means that we are designing solutions with incomplete data.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It can also lead to men criticising or undermining gender equality and to men feeling excluded, abandoned, or left behind in the debate about gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure that many of my hon parliamentarian colleagues have heard of Mr Andrew Tate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Tate is a 37 year old English-American influencer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: He had over 8.5 million followers on X, formerly Twitter, and his TikTok videos have been viewed 11.6 billion times.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In his videos, Mr Tate says that women belong in the home, cannot drive and are a man's property; women deserve to be physically, sexually and emotionally abused; and that sexual assault victims share responsibility for their assaults.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Despite claiming that many of his comments were intended as a joke and have been taken out of context, his popularity on social media clearly shows that people are listening to him.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, Mr Speaker, I strongly suspect that many of these people are men and boys.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, I am not in any way shying away from the fact that it is overwhelmingly women who bear the burden of gender inequality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is women who are constantly over-represented in data about disadvantage, prejudice and violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The purpose of highlighting the impact on men is not to negate the impact of gender inequality on women, nor to excuse men for what can be appalling and dangerous attitudes and behaviour, but to let men know that they will also be better off if we address gender inequality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men die younger than women, and have higher rates of heart disease, stroke and diabetes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men have higher rates of alcohol and substance abuse, are more frequently the victims and perpetrators of violent crime, drive dangerously and die in car accidents more often, are less likely to seek personal or health support and engage in risk-taking behaviour both in public and at work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men also have far higher rates of self-harm and suicide.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: To address traditional gender norms and the construction of masculinity, we need to talk with men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am doing so, because it is important that men recognise that they too will benefit from a culture of gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: At present, far too many men think that gender equality is only relevant to women, or worse, that gender equality is making things worse for men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They benefit personally, through enhanced physical and emotional health and well-being.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men benefit from more fulfilling and successful personal relationships with their wives and children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Greater flexibility with respect to gender-based roles, responsibilities and norms within relationships, assists relationships to become more egalitarian and more emotionally and physically fulfilling for both partners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Most men want the women in their lives to be safe from harassment and abuse, to be able to pursue a career of choice and to be treated and paid the same as their male counterparts, and to find love in relationship that is based on mutual respect and genuine partnership.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to harness the inherent protectiveness that men frequently have towards women, without inadvertently reinforcing the unhelpful notion that women are helpless creatures who cannot survive without a man, or that women should be placed on a pedestal and treated as a possession.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men also benefit from friendships, communities and workplaces with greater gender diversity and equality, and from the invaluable and unique perspectives and contributions that women bring to these systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men can learn a great deal from women, just as women can learn a great deal from men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, of course, Mr Speaker, men benefit from lower rates of incarceration and criminal or social sanctions due to problematic or unlawful behaviour towards women, including physical and sexual assault and abuse, and domestic violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: A culture of gender equality will assist to make Singapore's institutions, businesses and workplaces more representative, and therefore more productive and profitable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, a culture of gender equality will assist to create a society where relationships between all people, including between men and women, are based on respect, fairness and equity, rather than an outdated and dangerous power-based norms on stereotypes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Mao Zedong is frequently quoted as saying: "Women hold up half the sky".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In an ideal word this is true, however, in reality, I suspect that the ratio is not so equal or fair.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: First and foremost, we need to respectfully, effectively and comprehensively engage with boys and men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to talk with men, we need to listen to men and we need to support men to be part of the journey as we build a culture of gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men need to be and feel that they are equal and valued stakeholders in discussions and decisions about gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Boys are taught, observe and model gender stereotypes and norms at a very early age, while at home, at school, in sport and in public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: If we want to influence how boys turn into men in Singapore, we need to start early.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And I do not mean just telling boys about what is right and wrong but sitting down with boys and listening to them and learning from their views and opinions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Gender equality is not the responsibility of other men, it is the responsibility of all men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need more men, including men in positions of authority, influence and respect to be role models and ambassadors for gender equality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Business leaders, politicians, teachers, coaches, and sport and music stars – all can have a significant impact on shifting the attitudes and behaviours of other men and boys.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As part of being a role model and ambassador, we need more men to step forward and state publicly and proudly how they can do things differently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I call on my hon male colleagues in the Chamber today to step forward and be part of this campaign.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While women are, without a doubt, at substantial and disproportionate disadvantage as a result of gender norms, they also have an important role to play in challenging and addressing gender norms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: One important aspect of this role is for women to be vigilant about either deliberately or inadvertently reinforcing the notion of toxic masculinity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While many men do need to change their attitudes and behaviour towards women, it is unhelpful if the only message that men get are that gender inequality is their fault and that everything they do is wrong or inadequate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is also unhelpful for women to deliberately adopt or reinforce gender stereotypical norms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Just like men, women also need reflect on how they may be contributing to gender inequality and how they can do things differently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, most people have not even heard of the "HEAL" professions: health, education, administration and literacy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Doing so not only assists break down traditional gender roles, which is, in itself, a benefit, it also opens up a suite of currently unavailable career options and roles for men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This is a good thing for men; it is a good thing for women; and it is a good thing for Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Traditional gender roles can be deeply entrenched and may take many years of coordinated whole-of-Government policy and practice guidance to shift.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, the framework would also detail how men and boys, and women and girls, of all ages and backgrounds will be meaningfully involved the development and ongoing implementation of the framework.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is time for the men and women of Singapore to stand together to hold up the sky.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Almost exactly two years ago, we had a nine-and-a-half-hour debate on the Motion on the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The White Paper, with its 25 action plans, was unanimously endorsed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members shared their views and hopes for moving Singapore towards a fairer and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I was very encouraged by what Member of Parliament Louis Ng said then, and I quote, "that the action plans in the White Paper are good not only for women, but also for men, as they steer our society towards a healthier, fairer set of norms, cultures and practices".

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From the very start, the Singapore Government has treated women as the equal half of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Women's Charter, which was passed in 1961, instituted the equal standing of men and women in marriage and ensured the welfare and protection of women and girls in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since then, our policies on education, housing, employment, healthcare, and access to justice have been and continue to be gender-neutral.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Both men and women have equal access to opportunities and social support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our laws on issues such as protection from violence and harm, and the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation, apply to both men and women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government believes in the fundamental equality between persons and strives to create a society where all can pursue their aspirations freely and fully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singapore was ranked amongst the top 10 again this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are very proud of this recognition as the GII is a composite measure of gender inequality along three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment – in terms of education and participation in politics – and the labour market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, we recognise that there is still work to be done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We embarked on the nationwide "Conversations on Singapore Women Development" in 2020 to hear Singaporeans' views on the challenges and aspirations of Singapore women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Importantly, through the process, the Government made it clear that women's development and progress is not at the expense of men – but in partnership with men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Out of the nearly 6,000 Singaporeans who participated in these Conversations, one-fifth were men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Prof Razwana on the need to listen to men, and engage and support them to be part of this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Men are equally constrained by societal expectations of how they should behave or perform at home, or at work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We should recognise everyone’s individuality and intrinsic worth, so that more men and women can be empowered to realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last month, I delivered the opening remarks at the Singapore side-event on Singapore's whole-of-society partnership to transform mindsets at the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a key inter-governmental platform for UN member states and Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) to come together to discuss important issues on women’s development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Xander Ong, CEO of Centre for Fathering, was one of the panelists at the side event.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Xander’s participation at a CSW exemplifies the fact that in Singapore, we believe that changing mindsets on gender roles matters too and requires the partnership of both men and women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Xander spoke passionately about equal partnerships in parenting and sharing caregiving responsibilities in the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are clear signs that men in Singapore are stepping up to play a role to make our society a fairer and more inclusive one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share about further steps we are taking to build a culture for gender equality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The journey to shift mindsets towards gender stereotypes and roles starts from the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents are our first role models and examples of partnership and respect between men and women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As parents, it is our responsibility to pass down and instil in our children the right values of respect between men and women, and be role models ourselves through our actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am heartened that we are seeing positive mindset shifts towards active fathering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many studies, internationally and in Singapore, have also shown that children with more involved fathers have better developmental outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is committed to helping fathers achieve their family aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I hope we can work towards a society where it is just as natural for fathers to take paternity leave and shared parental leave, so that both fathers and mothers can support their children in their early years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With men taking a more active role in caregiving within the family, we hope that over time this will help to shift gender roles within the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This would also encourage more equal sharing of caregiving responsibilities, towards elderly family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that women are currently taking up a larger proportion of the caregiving burden.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The journey of changing mindsets starts with the family, but does not end there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In schools, the Government has enhanced our Character and Citizenship Education curriculum to address gender stereotypes and teach our children and youth the values of respect and appropriate behaviours in school to shape healthy social norms from young.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also provide our students with Education and Career Guidance to explore a variety of education and career pathways based on their interests and strengths, and to not be limited by gender stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am heartened to note that women comprise close to 40% of students studying STEM in our tertiary institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2020, women also make up 41% of our tech workforce, higher than the global average of 28%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Prof Razwana spoke about empowering men to join the "HEAL", or the Health, Education, Administration and Literacy, professions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are seeing a higher proportion of men in the nursing profession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The proportion of male nurses registered with the Singapore Nursing Board has increased, from 8.5% in 2011 to 12% in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, the number of male preschool educators has increased by about 30% from 185 in 2021 to about 245 persons today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, male preschool educators still make up less than 1% of the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue our efforts to attract talents, both men and women, into growing sectors such as healthcare and education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also encouraging flexible work arrangements (FWAs) as a workplace norm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will make it easier for employees, both men and women, to request for FWAs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To empower both women and men to better manage their family and work commitments, we have doubled the number of childcare places, and we recently announced the pilot infant childminding scheme, to provide parents with more options to care for their infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond legislation and policies, each of us can do our part to foster fair, inclusive, and progressive workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Employers can implement corporate initiatives to empower women at the workplace and nurture qualified women to undertake leadership roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is heartening to see more corporate initiatives to nurture women talent, many of which are championed by men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Managers and colleagues can support and help facilitate the re-entry of mothers back to the workforce after taking a break in their career.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must be equally supportive of fathers who need to take leave to care for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the community, we work with our partners and stakeholders to make Singapore a safe and empowering place for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We note Prof Razwana's point that harmful gender norms can have a profound impact on violent and abusive behaviour by men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A Singapore civil society organisation, United Women Singapore, runs a "Boys Empowered" programme that creates a safe space for males to have conversations on healthy masculinity, male allyship, personal boundaries and the concept of gender stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It also equips them with skills to de-escalate and prevent situations of violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Next month, I will be leading an Inter-Ministerial Committee to present our 6th Periodic Report to the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, or CEDAW in short.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will present the progress that Singapore has made since our last review in 2017.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The CEDAW Committee, comprising 23 experts, will assess Singapore’s compliance with the CEDAW Convention to protect and empower women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will put our best foot forward and present Singapore’s efforts, developments and achievements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will not rest on our laurels and will continue to strengthen efforts towards gender equality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But the intent of the White Paper exercise goes beyond policy and legislation; we cannot force a culture of gender equality through legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Rather, it aims to engender consciousness among Singaporeans on what all of us can do to help each other lead fulfilling lives, where a Singaporean, whether male or female, can pursue their aspirations freely and fully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Changing mindsets on gender roles requires the partnership of both men and women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this partnership starts in the family, continues in our schools, workplaces and in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must work together across the whole-of-society, across all domains to change minds, change norms and change lives.
